#4569. Tesla wants its sworn Cybercab answers to NHTSA kept entirely secret

Tesla has answered NHTSA’s Special Order demanding it prove, under oath, that the Cybercab meets federal safety standards. The response landed on the October 30 deadline, and Tesla asked the agency to keep all of it confidential.

The only part of the filing the public can read is a 30-page guide for firefighters. Everything about how a car with no steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors was certified as compliant is blacked out.

We reported in September that NHTSA had ordered Tesla to show its work on the Cybercab’s certification. The order came one week after the company started charging for Cybercab rides in Austin on September 3 and put 21 questions to the company, with civil penalties of up to $139 million for an incomplete answer and criminal exposure for a false one.

Tesla first tried to buy time. On September 18, it asked for eight more weeks, until November 20, citing “the voluminous nature of the request” and the work of searching its records and writing “thorough narrative formats in response to each question.” NHTSA gave it 30 days instead. The new deadline was October 30, and Tesla met it.

Three Tesla documents now sit in the AQ26002 docket, and two of them are empty.

The first is Tesla’s response letter, dated October 30 and addressed from 1 Tesla Road in Austin. It is one page long. The only text is: “The entirety of this file is confidential business information.”

The second is a placeholder for Tesla’s answer to Request 8, which asked the company to explain, standard by standard, how it determined the Cybercab complies: which subpart it certified to, and whether it ran physical tests, simulations, or engineering analyses. Per NHTSA’s note, the responsive documents carry a confidentiality request “for the entirety of each document.”

The third is the only substantive document: Tesla’s Cybercab First Responder Interaction Plan, version 1.2, dated September 3. It’s a real document with useful information in it. It’s also something Tesla has had on its website since July, aimed at police and fire crews, not regulators.

So the public gets a tow-truck manual, and the certification argument stays sealed.

The Special Order wasn’t a fishing expedition. It named the rules the Cybercab doesn’t obviously meet, and it seeks to understand how Tesla believes it can get around it.

FMVSS 135 says “the service brakes shall be activated by means of a foot control.” NHTSA has stated in public that a manufacturer of a vehicle with no foot brake can’t certify to it, then asked Tesla how it did. FMVSS 108 requires a turn-signal control that cancels itself when the steering wheel turns. FMVSS 111 requires mirrors. And the agency wanted to know whether Tesla certified the car with temporary driver controls bolted in and then removed them, which would run into the Safety Act’s “make inoperative” prohibition.

It also asked how the Cybercab is legal without a Part 555 exemption, the route Amazon’s Zoox took for its own steering-wheel-less robotaxi in July. Zoox applied, made its case, and got an exemption capped at 2,500 vehicles a year. Tesla self-certified and started charging for rides.

Every one of those answers is now under a confidentiality claim.

The first-responder plan was written for a different audience, but it brushes against several of NHTSA’s questions.

It says the Cybercab is “not typically equipped with a steering wheel or acceleration and brake pedals.” The word “typically” is doing work there. The same document notes that a Cybercab with a steering wheel and pedals “is typically an engineering or test vehicle, and operates at SAE Level 2 autonomy,” and includes instructions for driving one. That’s relevant to Requests 5 through 7, which asked whether the subject vehicles can be driven with temporarily attached controls.

It describes an operational design domain covering “all public roadways, such as freeways, highways, city streets, and rural roads,” at all hours, in light and moderate rain, fog, and snow. That is a far wider envelope than the Austin geofence the cars run in today, and it references an “Arizona Areas of Operation Appendix.” Request 1 asked for the ODD and Request 2 for scaling plans.

And it confirms that first responders can be granted access to on-board touchscreen controls to move the car, after showing a badge to the B-pillar camera (that’s interesting). Request 20 asked whether the touchscreen can move the vehicle and under what restrictions.

Nothing in it touches brakes, mirrors, telltales, or the certification itself.

Confidentiality requests go to NHTSA’s Chief Counsel under Part 512. The agency decides whether Tesla’s claim holds, and it can order a public version released if it doesn’t. NHTSA hasn’t said anything about the request, and it hasn’t found the Cybercab noncompliant with any standard.

This is familiar. In June 2025, Tesla asked NHTSA to hide its answers about the original Robotaxi launch in Austin, a service running on supervised FSD while FSD was under investigation. Those answers never surfaced.

NHTSA’s opening resume for the audit put the affected population at about 1,000 vehicles. The Cybercab is still carrying passengers in Austin while the agency reads a filing nobody else can.

I don't see how the answers can have confidential business secrets. It is about meeting public safety standards, not asking for schematics, technical details or designs. It is about clear public safety requirement and how the vehicle qualify as meeting it.

The so called keyword from Tesla's self certification is "applicable". Tesla may argue that many of those requirements aren't applicable in their test vehicle. But I would like to see the justifications on that.

Tesla’s position in September was that the Cybercab complies with every applicable federal standard, including the one that requires a brake pedal. If that’s true, the argument for it is the most interesting document in the autonomous vehicle industry right now, and Tesla just asked the government to make sure nobody reads it.

We get why a company redacts test data and supplier details. But the legal theory for how a car with no foot brake meets a foot-brake rule doesn’t sound like a trade secret to me. Zoox’s exemption petition is public. Waymo’s safety framework is public. Tesla’s case for why it didn’t need to ask is sealed, cover letter included.

NHTSA now has to decide whether “the entirety of this file” is really confidential business information. If it says no, we’ll finally see how Tesla certified this car. If it says yes, about 1,000 Cybercabs keep driving on a certification the public isn’t allowed to check.

#4568. Driven: The Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Won’t Make You Wait

The Mercedes-AMG GT55 and GT63 EVs bring Formula 1 battery technology to the road.

The most shocking thing about the new Mercedes-AMG GT63 4-Door Coupe isn’t its 1475 pound-feet of torque or its 1153 horsepower. Or the estimated 2.0-second run to 60 mph. Or the flat cornering. Or the responsive steering. Or the drive modes that let you change how the GT doles out its three-motor grunt. It isn’t even the polarizing style. It’s that this car charges at at a rate of up to 600 kilowatts.

That kind of power makes replenishing the battery almost as quick as pumping gas. Mercedes says its new GT will go from 10 to 80 percent in just 11 minutes. In a demonstration we witnessed, the car was still pulling 259 kilowatts at 78 percent state of charge. Impressive stuff.

Of course, finding a 600-kW charger in the U.S. is another story. In Europe, these kinds of high-high-power DC chargers are increasing in popularity thanks to a growing quantity of heavy electric trucks. But even if you can’t find a charger that can provide more than 350 kW of juice, the GT63—and its less powerful sibling, the 805-hp GT55—can max that charger out for much longer than an EV with a 350-kW peak. As you might expect, both GT variants will come to the U.S. with NACS plugs.

See all results for new 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door EV for sale near 20147

The 2027 GT 4-Door can do this thanks to a thermal strategy borrowed from Formula 1. The car’s 106-kWh battery pack, which consists of 2660 cells arranged in 18 modules, is oil cooled. The terminals of the individual cells are where the heat really builds during charging, and by using a cooling loop that focuses on those terminals first, engineers can pump more power into the battery without damaging the cells. This method keeps temps stable across the entire battery within a range of about 9 degrees.

EPA ranges are still TBD, but we expect both the GT55 and GT63 to break 300 miles in maximum-range configuration. Wheels and tires will play a role as they always do, but we mention a max-range config because the GT 4-Door packs a couple of optional active aerodynamic elements to boost range. A hidden front panel works in concert with an extendable rear diffuser, because extending the body’s total length reduces drag. (It’s also really interesting when the diffuser extends several inches beyond the rear bumper.) There are also some moving elements under the body work that increase downforce, but those are more for corner carving than for hypermiling. And, of course, the wing out back can adjust to reduce drag or increase downforce, depending on driving behavior.

The higher-zoot GT63 also comes packed with all manner of newfangled suspension hardware. Hydraulic anti-roll control and air springs support multilink geometries front and rear. All the suspension components are aluminum, except for the two rear upper links, which are stamped steel. The lower-power 55 gets conventional anti-roll bars instead of the hydraulic ones. Rear-axle steer, which can turn the rear rollers up to 6 degrees in either direction, is standard.

See all results for new 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door EV for sale near 20147

Another clever addition is the use of aramid in the crash structure, a synthetic fiber you might recognize from its use in bulletproof vests. AMG lashes aramid rope (roughly the diameter of a hearty man’s pinkie finger) to the longitudinal chassis rails. In the event that the car hits a pole or a tree, the rope transfers the load to the chassis, and those longitudinal members crumple inward a bit, hopefully preventing the impact from involving the undoubtedly expensive front motor.

“Structural frunk” is a phrase we’re still getting used to saying out loud. The AMG GT 4-Door has a small frunk, yes, but it’s best used to store a charging cable or other small knickknacks you want to keep handy. Unlike your typical plastic frunk, though, this one is made of carbon fiber. The box bolts directly to the chassis, and it’s stiff enough that it boosts the torsional rigidity of the front end by 35 percent. It is also curved to direct airflow under the hood, so it has three purposes. (Serving as an ersatz beverage cooler does not count as a fourth.)

The AMG Dynamic Package, which is standard on the GT63 and optional on the GT55, brings three control knobs labeled Response, Agility, and Traction to the center console. These knobs, called Race Engineer, have a profound effect on the car’s behavior. The Response knob, available in all drive modes, plays with the accelerator calibration. Position one is a very lazy “throttle”; acceleration ramps up almost comically slowly. On the other side, position nine is a light switch. The Agility knob, which is only active in Sport, Sport+, and Race modes with stability control turned off, works in concert with what remains of the stability control, the front-to-rear torque split, and the rear-axle torque vectoring. Position one maintains a tight line, while nine allows for lurid drifts. The Traction knob, also only active in Sport, Sport+, and Race modes with stability control turned off, is pretty self-explanatory; nine almost eliminates the traction assist entirely.

Tinkering with these three knobs generates vastly different results. If you want to work on your driving line around a track, keep the Agility and Response knobs in positions one through three. The car keeps the body tight and perfectly meters power on corner exit. Crank them to seven or higher, and you’ll meet your new best friend: oversteer. Just mash the throttle and keep the front tires pointed where you want to go, and Race Engineer will handle the rest.

Sport+ is the only mode where fake powertrain sounds are pumped into the cabin. In addition to that synthetic soundtrack, a tachometer appears on the instrument screen, and the steering-wheel paddles change jobs from adjusting brake-regen levels to working virtual gears. The V-8 rumble, which includes shakers in the front seats, is based on the last-gen AMG GT R and manages a solid impersonation. Shifts arrive with an abrupt but brief interruption in torque; sure, the feeling is probably more pronounced than what’s felt from the actual GT R’s dual-clutch, but the theatrics are executed perfectly.

With the Agility and Response knobs set to seven, the GT63 drives much smaller than its 119.7-inch wheelbase and 5500-pound curb weight imply. Turn-in is crisp, and adroit steering corrections result in quick responses. You can even trail-brake this big car deep into corners while the Race Engineer algorithms help with rotation.

Driving around town, the GT55 is limited to 557 horses and the GT63 to 711, but a quick hop over to Race mode will call up all the remaining horses. Should you desire short periods of naughty driving, a boost mode achieves the same full-power blast, albeit in 55- and 63-second bursts (you can guess which model gets which duration). It’s not like you need four figures’ worth of horsepower to make a pass on a mountain road, but passengers will surely love it. Both variants are quiet and smooth riding, though not quite as smooth as an Active Ride–equipped Porsche Taycan.

Figuring out where the AMG lands among other high-power EV sedans will have to wait for a comparison test, but our first sampling indicates that the Merc splits the difference between the more spacious Lucid Air and the smaller Taycan. The GT’s interior is top-spec Mercedes, full of great materials and clever ergonomic touches. There’s a fair amount of customization through the central display, our favorite of which is the ability to rearrange and even hide some of the functions on the steering wheel knobs. Residents of Phoenix, for example, can remove Slippery mode from the mode-switching dial. Degenerates can set the dial to only include Comfort and Race. The sky’s the limit.

The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT55 goes on sale later this year with a starting price of $146,550, undercutting the driver-focused Taycan GTS. When the 63 hits dealers next year for $176,550, it’ll likewise undercut on the Porsche Taycan Turbo. With this level of performance on board—both the charging and the hard-charging kind—the GT 4-Door should be quite a strong competitor.

#4567. Raccoon with an arrow stuck in her face rescued in Massachusetts

Published Nov 7, 2026 10:06 AM EST

Earlier this week, wildlife veterinarian Dr. Priya Patel and her colleagues at the Cape Wildlife Center in Barnstable, Massachusetts had to deal with something they had never seen before: a raccoon with an arrow sticking out of its face.

But the saga really began several days before then, when an individual in Plymouth, Massachusetts called the Cape Wildlife Center to let them know that they had spotted the injured raccoon. The wildlife center team told the caller to contact the local animal control to apprehend the raccoon, who had no intention of making it easy.

It took animal control around one week to catch the trash panda. Patel, who is also the medical director of the wildlife center, tells Popular Science that she was a “very feisty raccoon,” even while inside of her cage. “So we decided to sedate her right away in the cage so that there was less stress for her, and then we were safe getting her out.”

Once the snoozing raccoon had been removed from the cage, the team realized that whatever was sticking out of her face was also sticking out the back of her head. Patel and her colleagues quickly took X-ray images, which revealed the obvious shape of an arrow—possibly a mini crossbow arrow. In her misfortune, the feisty raccoon was actually incredibly lucky. The arrow hadn’t touched her eye or sinus cavity, nor had it fractured her skull.

“We were able to quickly assess that there was no major structural damage to her, and then we were able to remove it,” Patel explains. “And so we cleaned the wound and put some antibiotic ointment on it and started her on antibiotics and paint meds. She just got really lucky, and we were just grateful to Plymouth animal control for not giving up on trying to catch her.”

The raccoon is doing well, and will stay at the wildlife center until the wound heals properly and she completes a course of antibiotics. The team then expects to return her to the wild.

In Massachusetts, it is legal to hunt raccoons. In 2026, the raccoon and opossum hunting season was from January 1 to January 31, and from October 2026 through the end of the year.

We break down the best car seats for safety, comfort, and everyday convenience to help you find the right fit for your family.

This article will be updated periodically with new information.

Choosing the right car seat is one of the most important decisions you’ll make as a parent, but sorting through dozens of models, safety features, and installation systems can quickly become overwhelming. From infant carriers to convertible seats, the best options balance safety, comfort, ease of use, and a secure fit in your vehicle.

While all car seats sold in the U.S. must meet federal safety standards, not every seat is equally suited to every family. We looked at top-rated models, practical features, and everyday usability to help narrow down the choices, whether you’re bringing home a newborn, upgrading for a growing toddler, or preparing for the next stage.

More Car Related Gear for Kids: Best Ride-on Electric Cars for Kids | Gifts for Boys | Best Lego Car Sets

Buying one car seat that can handle nearly every stage of childhood is appealing, especially when it doesn’t sacrifice convenience. With four configurations, rear-facing, forward-facing, high-back booster, and backless booster, the Graco 4Ever DLX is designed to serve families for up to 10 years. That versatility, combined with its practical features, makes it our Top Pick.

Graco’s InRight Latch connectors click into place, while an integrated belt lock-off helps simplify seatbelt installation. The 10-position headrest adjusts alongside the no-rethread harness, and six recline positions accommodate growing passengers. The RapidRemove machine-washable cover is another welcome feature, allowing parents to tackle accident, spills, and other kid messes without uninstalling the seat.

The 4Ever DLX is relatively bulky, and its 40-pound rear-facing limit falls short of some competitors. Still, its four-stage versatility, easy adjustments, and thoughtful design make it an excellent all-around choice for families.

The Maxi-Cosi Pria All-in-One delivers impressive versatility for the price, making it a smart investment for parents who want one car seat to last through multiple stages of childhood. It accommodates children from 5 to 40 pounds rear-facing, 30 to 65 pounds forward-facing, and 40 to 100 pounds in booster mode, eliminating the need to purchase separate seats as your child grows.

Convenience is another selling point. The one-click Latch connectors simplify installation, while the QuikFit headrest and harness adjust together without rethreading. Three recline positions, plush infant inserts, and breathable fabrics help keep passengers comfortable on longer drives. Machine-washable upholstery and dishwasher-safe cupholders are especially welcome given accidents are inevitable with kids.

The Pria is relatively bulky, so smaller vehicles may present fit challenges. Still, its comfort, adjustability, and long-term usability make it an excellent value compared with pricier convertible models.

A compelling case for spending more on a car seat is Britax’s One4Life Slim, especially if you prioritize easy installation and long-term versatility. Its standout feature is Britax’s ClickTight installation system, which uses the vehicle’s seat belt to secure the seat without the usual wrestling match. At just 17.5 inches wide, its slimmer profile also makes it practical for families with limited back-seat space.

Designed to accommodate children from 5 to 120 pounds across rear-facing, forward-facing, and high-back booster configurations, the One4Life Slim offers years of use. The 50-pound rear-facing limit is especially appealing for parents who want to keep their children rear-facing longer. A no-rethread harness, adjustable headrest, and machine-washable cover add convenience.

It’s heavier and considerably more expensive than basic convertible seats, but the One4Life Slim is designed to handle nearly every stage without complicating life for new parents.

Extended rear-facing capability and strong independent crash-test results make the UPPAbaby Rove a compelling option for parents moving beyond an infant car seat. It supports children from 14 to 50 pounds rear-facing and 30 to 65 pounds forward-facing, offering years of use without an immediate upgrade as your child grows.

UPPAbaby’s QuickGuard installation system features spring-loaded belt lock-offs, while the SmartSecure indicator changes from red to green to help confirm proper installation. This is extremely helpful and honestly puts a parents mind at ease if their child is secure.

A multidirectional tether, side-impact protection pods, and energy-absorbing foam add to its safety-focused design. The no-rethread harness, five recline positions, and removable, machine-washable cushioning make adjustments and cleanup more manageable.

The Rove has earned excellent crash-protection marks, although testers found its bulky dimensions and installation challenging in some vehicles. It’s also unsuitable for newborns under 14 pounds. Still, its extended rear-facing limits and thoughtful features make it a strong contender for convertible seats.

For new parents, a car seat that’s easy to install correctly and convenient to carry can make a difference in daily life. Chicco’s KeyFit 35 delivers on both fronts, combining practical safety features with a detachable carrier that works with compatible Chicco strollers. That’s a win-win.

Designed for infants weighing 4 to 35 pounds and measuring up to 32 inches tall, the KeyFit 35 features Chicco’s SuperCinch Latch tightener, LockSure seat-belt lock-off, and built-in leveling indicators to simplify installation. An anti-rebound bar adds another layer of protection, while the no-rethread harness and adjustable headrest accommodate growing babies.

Chicco’s reputation is rooted in easy installation and reliable use for everyday. The carrier weighs about 10 pounds, and its infant-only design means you’ll eventually need a convertible seat. Still, its convenience, stroller compatibility, and details make this is an excellent choice for a baby’s first car seat.

Car seats aren’t one-size-fits-all. Infant seats are designed exclusively for rear-facing use, while convertible and all-in-one models accommodate children through multiple stages. Pay close attention to the manufacturer’s height and weight limits, not age alone. The NHTSA recommends keeping children rear-facing as long as possible, until they reach the seat’s maximum rear-facing height or weight limit.

Even highly rated car seats won’t work equally well in every vehicle. Check your owner’s manual for approved seating positions and installation instructions, and consider how much space the seat takes up, especially in smaller cars. If you have multiple children, width matters even more. Whenever possible, test the seat in your vehicle before you buy it.

A properly installed car seat is essential, and complicated installation systems can lead to mistakes and stress. Look for clear leveling indicators, accessible belt paths, and user-friendly LATCH connectors or seatbelt lock-offs. Remember, LATCH isn’t necessarily safer than a seat belt used correctly. A certified Child Passenger Safety Technician can also help verify your installation.

Think beyond the initial purchase. Machine-washable covers, adjustable harnesses, removable cupholders, and stroller compatibility can make daily use considerably easier. All-in-one seats offer long-term value, but infant carriers are often more convenient for newborns. Check expiration dates, manufacturer warranties, and how long your child can realistically use each configuration before deciding which features justify the price.

The safest car seat is one that fits your child’s height and weight, installs correctly in your vehicle, and is used properly every time. All new car seats sold in the U.S. must meet federal safety standards, but independent crash testing and ease-of-use ratings can help distinguish models. For newborns, choose a rear-facing infant or convertible seat approved for their size.

NHTSA recommends keeping children rear-facing until they reach the maximum height or weight limit specified by their car seat’s manufacturer. Many convertible seats accommodate rear-facing children up to 40 or 50 pounds, letting them stay in this safer position well beyond their second birthday.

Replace a car seat when your child exceeds its height or weight limits, the seat reaches its expiration date, or it has been involved in a moderate or severe crash. NHTSA advises that seats involved in minor crashes may not need replacement if they meet specific criteria. Always check the manufacturer’s instructions and inspect the seat for damage or missing components.

Infant car seats are designed for rear-facing use and typically feature detachable carriers that make transporting newborns easier. Convertible car seats stay installed in the vehicle and accommodate children through the rear-facing and forward-facing stages. Infant seats offer greater portability, while convertible models generally provide better long-term value. The best choice depends on your vehicle, budget, and daily routine.

#4565. Hyundai is recalling nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to an airbag software defect

Hyundai issued a recall affecting nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to a software error that could cause the airbag to fail to deploy in a crash.

In a letter sent to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on November 4, Hyundai said it was recalling certain 2019 to 2023 Kona Electric and 2019 to 2022 Veloster N vehicles.

The recall impacts 37,901 vehicles in total, including 29,058 Kona Electric and 8,843 Veloster N models.

According to documents submitted to the NHTSA, the issue stems from a software error with the airbag control unit (ACU) that can cause the airbag malfunction indicator light (MIL) to come on and the airbag system to deactivate under certain driving conditions.

The data may become corrupted during a system reboot or power interruption while the system is writing to the ACU’s memory. When this happens, the airbag MIL will illuminate to warn drivers.

As of October 22, 2026, Hyundai is aware of 331 alleged incidents related to the issue. However, none have resulted in a crash, fire, or injury.

Owners can take their vehicle to the closest dealer, where it will update the ACU software, free of charge.

Hyundai expects to mail out owner notification letters on January 1, 2027. In the meantime, owners can contact Hyundai’s customer service at 1-855-371-9460 with any questions or concerns. Hyundai’s recall number is 311.

You can also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 or visit the NHTSA.gov website for more information. The NHTSA campaign number is 26V728.

#4563. Troublesome black bear Nugget wins the 2026 Annoying Sibling Award

Published Nov 7, 2026 12:32 PM EST

Anyone who has brothers and sisters knows that siblings can be your greatest allies and biggest foes all at once. The same principle appears to apply to bear siblings.

A small black bear (Ursus americanus) named Nugget demonstrated that all too well this summer. Nugget is known for his very small stature, a fur pattern that looks like goggles around his eyes, and a reddish coat that shifts to black later in the summer. He also likes to get up in his siblings business.

Over the summer, the U.S. Forest Service team at Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska watched Nugget jabbing at his very patient and bigger sibling Crescent. For these antics, Nugget officially won the 2026 Annoying Sibling Award.

“This scene went on for almost 30 minutes. Each time Nugget would slowly creep out and touch Crescent and then they’d seem to play fight,” the rangers write. “It was like watching two siblings fight until the bigger sibling had enough. Well managed ecosystems and recreation sites on national forests like the Tongass provide unique opportunities to witness scenes like this.”

The rangers at Tongass National Forest are currently awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendanhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. The run is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Like their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of what they are up to 24/7.

#4560. Ford Mustang Dark Horse Driver Leads Police on Wild Chase Through Los Angeles Before Crash

The driver couldn't outrun the cops—but his passenger, apparently fresh out of jail for felony evading, insisted he could have.

Los Angeles County’s fabled Mulholland Drive is the perfect place to enjoy a Ford Mustang Dark Horse. Packed with tight curves, dramatic views, and homes owned by the rich and famous, the scenic route is one of the most famous roads in America. However, one Ford Mustang driver and his boastful passenger allegedly decided to turn it into a setting for a high-speed police chase.

According to reports by Fox 11 Los Angeles and The California Post, the pursuit began shortly after 1 a.m. on Thursday, November 5. Police reportedly had reason to believe that the Mustang was stolen, although authorities later specified that it was not. But their attempt to pull it over kicked off a chase that lasted nearly a half hour, with the Ford reportedly hitting speeds of about 80 miles per hour.

The driver reportedly didn’t stick to Mulholland Drive; he also jumped on Highway 101 and then Interstate 405, before eventually losing control and crashing on Woodcliff Road in Sherman Oaks. Authorities say that despite being injured, the driver tried to flee on foot after the crash but was quickly caught. The passenger was also detained, and he had some words for the police. “I just got out of the joint for felony evading,” the passenger told authorities, as captured on video. “If I was driving, you wouldn’t have caught me, I swear to God.”

In any event, the passenger was released after police questioned him. As for his buddy behind the wheel? He’s now facing felony evading charges of his own. A 500-horsepower Mustang Dark Horse may be made to eat up corners, but if those corners are on Mulholland Drive in the middle of the night—with police officers behind, no less—it might be better to keep those horses in the stable.

#4559. Meta-backed 250 MW solar farm breaks ground in Arkansas

Arkansas is getting another 250 megawatts (MW) of solar power, and Meta has signed up to buy it.

EDP Renewables North America (EDPR NA) broke ground on Cypress Knee Solar in Chicot County, in the southeastern corner of the state, on November 4. The solar farm is expected to be completed by 2028, bringing several hundred construction jobs and an estimated $25 million in county revenue over its lifetime.

Meta’s long-term power purchase agreement helps it work toward its pledge to match 100% of its annual electricity use with renewable energy generation. Don’t confuse that pledge with Meta powering its data centers with renewables around the clock, though – Facebook and Instagram’s parent company is also backing new gas plants to meet its growing power demand.

The companies announced the deal in May. Cypress Knee is their third clean-energy agreement, bringing the total capacity covered by Meta’s deals with EDPR NA to 545 MW.

“As energy demand continues to rise, projects like Cypress Knee Solar help strengthen grid reliability while creating jobs, generating meaningful local revenue, and delivering long-term benefits to the communities that host them,” said EDPR NA CEO Sandhya Ganapathy.

EDPR NA says it has already contributed more than $77,000 during project development, including money to restore the Lakeside High School greenhouse, resources for the Lakeside Robotics team, and funding for the Lake Village food pantry.

#4558. 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Test: Capability, Comfort, and Style

With two new small-block V-8s, a new interior, and a wide-ranging trim lineup, the Silverado covers pickup needs from towing to dune jumps.

In ancient times, trucks were tools for farmers and construction workers. The idea that they should offer amenities like air conditioning or power steering would have been questionable, and the suggestion of heated seats or ambient lighting would have been laughed off the assembly line. We live in a gentler era, though, and the 2027 Chevy Silverado 1500 reflects the mainstream popularity of pickups for both work and play. Chevy’s half-ton lineup gets a major overhaul for the coming model year with reshaped sheetmetal; redesigned interiors featuring carbon fiber, wood, and bright pops of color; and two brand-new small-block V-8s that will delight internal-combustion loyalists.

Chevy has made enough changes to the Silverado for 2027 to call it a new generation, although what generation that is depends on if you’re starting your count from the first introduction of Silverado as its own model (1998) or all the way back to the first use of the name (1975, as a trim on the C/K models). We’re going from the ’90s, which would make this new truck the fifth generation. To earn its generational title, the Silverado wears a new exterior, crisp as a starched shirt, set off by LED lights, burly wheel lip moldings, and a redesigned bumper. Underneath, the chassis will be familiar from the previous year, albeit with some suspension tweaks for more stable towing and a better ride.

See all results for used cars for sale near 40203

The biggest news for truck fans won’t be the body styling or the interior decorating, but what’s under the big, angular hood. Lower trims still start out with an upgraded turbocharged 2.7-liter four-cylinder, now making 350 horsepower and 455 pound-feet of torque. Diesel fans get the returning Duramax turbo 3.0-liter inline-six, still rated at 305 horses and 495 pound-feet, but now with an optional 34-gallon fuel tank for a claimed (and bladder-challenging) 900-mile range.

And then there are the eight-cylinder stars of the show. These new V-8s are not bored-out versions of the outgoing 5.3- and 6.2-liter mills, but instead comprise completely new blocks, heads, intakes, and exhausts. The new engines measure out at 5.7 and 6.6 liters—or 346 and 401 cubic inches, for those speaking older tongues. Those designations were appealing enough to Chevrolet that they stamped them on the back of the aluminum blocks.

Most of our drive was divided between kitted-out High Country and rambunctious ZR2 models, both with the 6.6-liter, and we can report that the big small-block is powerful (481 ponies, 501 pound-feet), sonorous, and unexpectedly smooth, with elegant on-road manners and impressive trail performance. It’s also very quiet at idle, an effect of using newly added port fuel injection at low rpm and adding in direct injection as throttle input increases.

See all results for used cars for sale near 40203

Back at the C/D homestead, we spent time with the 402-hp, 428-lb-ft 5.7-liter V-8 in the lesser off-road-oriented Trail Boss trim. The Trail Boss is the light-beer equivalent of the hoppy ZR2, offering some trail tech without going all-in on off-road. A roughly two-inch suspension lift, 34-inch Goodyear Wrangler Territory MT tires on 18-inch wheels, and optional underbody cameras give the Trail Boss gravel-road cred. On the pavement, the Trail Boss rides with a little more rear-end jiggle than the High Country (with its adaptive dampers) or the ZR2 (with its Multimatic DSSV setup). At the test track, the Boss got to 60 mph in a reasonable 6.4 seconds and covered the quarter-mile in 14.6 seconds at its 94-mph top speed. But its dirt-focused rubber likely hampered its performance elsewhere. Braking from 70 mph took 198 feet and a twirl around the skidpad returned just 0.70 g of grip while fighting some unsurprising understeer.

In the real world, the Trail Boss felt quicker and more planted than its test results suggest, and the 5.7 offers nearly silent running (a mere 66 decibels and 21 sones at 70 mph). It’d better, given its $2690 option price. When combined with other options on our test truck, covering everything from multi-camera arrays to a slick coat of green paint, our mid-price model ended up with an as-tested window sticker of $76,795. That much scratch could get you into a rear-wheel-drive High Country model with the 5.7 or within spitting distance of a Duramax-equipped ZR2. Upgrading either of those trims to the 6.6-liter (not available on the Trail Boss) would require an extra $2505 for the ZR2 and $2800 for the High Country, with the latter also mandating an upgrade to 4WD. These new V-8s are slick but dear.

Even the base 2.7-liter work truck has a starting price of $40,045, but at least the lower trims benefit from some of the same features as the top-shelf models. The Silverado’s interior rework means that every 2027 truck showcases data on a 12.2-inch gauge cluster and a 16.3-inch center screen. ZR2 and High Country trims get an additional 11.5-inch passenger screen. The displays mark the return of Android Auto and Apple Car Play, but the system still includes Google built-in nav and search functions. We found the native navigation prone to directional confusion, so we’re glad GM walked back its plans to ditch phone mirroring.

The new GM UI is crisp and quick, but we had some issues with the touchscreen’s accuracy. Organizationally, the Silverado interior is scattered, with some controls on the left side of the dash, some in menus in the touchscreen, and some on hard buttons above the console. Chevy allows for menu customizations that create shortcuts to regularly used controls, but until a customer sets that up, they should be prepared for a hunt.

Dialing in the least-irritating combination of driver assist functions might take some time, but setting up for a proper truck job like towing will not. And it’ll handle a proper truck job: The new light-duty Chevy now boasts up to 13,700 pounds of max towing capacity (when properly equipped). The Silverado offers helpful setup and safety tech like a trailer brake-gain assistant for setting trailer brake proportions, as well as several split-view camera angles with overlay graphics that promise to make parking easier and prevent a jackknife. Super Cruise–equipped trucks can tow with the system running, although automatic lane changes are not available while towing.

The Silverado lineup includes everything from a regular cab with an extended cargo bed to the feature-heavy crew-cab top trims. The cabin is noticeably nicer than previous models, and the crew cab will comfortably fit a large, er, crew. Pickup trucks have changed a lot in the past century—largely for the better—but with increased comfort and capability come increased prices. No matter how good the Silverado’s two new V-8s are, there’s no way to drive around that truth.

#4557. Kia’s EV5 spotted with an updated design and a huge new infotainment display

Kia’s Sportage-sized electric SUV, the EV5, was spotted with a distinct new style and an overhauled interior, including a huge widescreen infotainment screen.

The EV5 is the fully electric SUV we want, but can’t have in the US. After launching it in China in 2023, Kia introduced the global version last year, which is now on sale in Europe, Canada, the UK, and other markets.

It has already been a big part of Kia’s comeback in China and is expected to become one of its best-selling EVs.

Kia appears to be preparing an updated version. A new EV5 model was recently spotted by ShortsCar in a South Korean parking garage without camouflage, and it’s expected to be the updated version.

You can see in the video that the design has changed quite a bit. Up front, the hood and headlights remain about the same, but new design elements like a black accent light are added.

It also features a unique bumper design, similar to that of the rugged EV5 WKNDR Concept Kia revealed last November at the Guangzhou Motor Show.

The biggest changes are inside, where the interior appears to be completely overhauled. Instead of the current large display screen spanning from the driver to the center, the new EV5 features a display that extends from the center to the passenger side.

There also appears to be an added slim display in front of the steering wheel. Since Hyundai has recently added a slim display to vehicles equipped with its Pleos infotainment system, the updated Kia EV5 is expected to feature the new setup.

However, this is still speculation and has not been confirmed. The center console has also changed. Instead of the physical buttons, it now has a cover, giving it a cleaner overall look.

According to a sticker on the back, the updated EV5 is set to launch in the Philippines. Given Kia initially launched the EV5 in China in 2023, it will be due for a facelift around 2027.

Kia has yet to confirm whether and when it will launch the updated EV5 in other global markets, such as Europe or Korea. It will likely arrive after the China-made version, like the current EV5. We should learn more details soon.

#4556. Yangwang U9 Xtreme Breaks Its Own Top Speed Record With 312.7-MPH One-Way Run

It’s the first production vehicle to surpass 500 kilometers per hour.

China’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme hypercar already held the record for fastest production car, but it seems the company wasn’t satisfied with that. The U9 Xtreme just beat itself—and crossed the 500 kilometer-per-hour barrier doing it.

With German racing driver Marc Bessing behind the wheel (the same man who piloted the car for its previous records), the U9 Xtreme hit 503.2 km/h during a run in Abu Dhabi on November 1. That’s 312.7 miles per hour. Unlike the previous record of 496.2 km/h (308.3 mph) that was set at Germany’s Papenberg track, this time, Yangwang took its electric hypercar to a closed public road; about six miles of Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed International Road was closed for the record run.

“Unlike a dedicated test track, a public road presents a different set of challenges, making precision, stability and confidence in the vehicle more important than ever,” Besseng said. “Breaking a world record once is extraordinary but doing it again in such a different environment is truly special.”

The road itself required sweeping prior to each run, and Yangwang spent two days running on the road before setting the record on the final pass. The company says it inspected every meter of the path for potential debris, even picking up rogue wire particles that could’ve been deposited from the cleaning brushes sweeping up.

Both the FIA and Guinness World Records have recognized the record as the highest speed achieved by a production car in a single-direction run. Updates to the car are credited for breaking the 500 km/h barrier versus last year’s 496.2 km/h run: Yangwang says it adjusted the angle of the rear wing to increase rear downforce, tweaked the suspension software to increase rebound damping “in response to subtle undulations in parts of the road,” and, changed tire pressure to increase high-speed stability.

In case you were wondering, the U9 Xtreme is fitted with four electric motors producing more than 2958 horsepower. It uses a 1200-volt battery pack, which is an upgrade over the regular U9’s 800-volt pack. As for the tire, Yangwang says it uses a specially designed tire from Giti Tire. Yangwang itself is a subsidiary of BYD, China’s largest automaker.

The next closest car to the U9 Xtreme is the Bugatti Chiron Super Sport that hit 304.8 mph back in 2019. In other words, Yangwang didn’t need to set this latest record to take back the crown. It simply ran the car for the love of the game, and of course to break that 500 km/h barrier.

The video is a fascinating watch, as Bessing spends plenty of time warming the tires and brakes before going for the run. He keeps it at about half or a little over half throttle until he gets past 380 km/h. From there on out, it’s full throttle as the car flies up to 480 km/h and creeps the rest of the way up to—and beyond—500 km/h.

#4554. Ford’s electric pickup is suddenly selling like hotcakes at 50% off used

Once America’s most popular electric pickup, the Ford F-150 Lightning is finding a second life on the used market.

The F-150 Lightning is hard to pass up at 50% to 60% off sticker price, even used. With new models no longer available, Ford’s electric pickup is suddenly selling like hotcakes on the used market.

After the last model rolled off the assembly line last December, CEO Jim Farley said the decision to end production came as the “very high-end EVs, the $50K, 70K, $80,000 vehicles, they just weren’t selling.”

At 50% to 60% off, it now looks like a bargain in the used market. “When Ford was selling it brand new, the math was complicated,” Jimmy Douglas, CEO of Plug, a wholesale EV dealer, recently told Bloomberg.

On the used market, however, “the Lightning is 50% to 60% of the sticker price and that is really a sweet spot,” he added.

Used Ford F-150 Lightnings are selling in about 20 days, less than half the 44-day average for used vehicles in the US. According to Edmunds.com, prices are now up 4% to about $50,000 since the start of the year.

Douglass said that close to one-third of used models are sold by rival dealerships that would normally flip them back to Ford. However, many are opting to sell them directly because of demand.

Chase Norris from Colorado called the electric pickup a bargain. He purchased a used Lightning for around $40,000 and considers it a major upgrade from his previous gas F-150.

EV Group CEO and cofounder Alex Lawrence, which sells pre-owned electric vehicles, said he can’t get his hands on any reasonably priced used F-150 Lightnings currently.

He said many Lightning buyers use it as a second truck to save money during their weekly commute.

It looks essentially the same as the gas-powered F-150, offers instant torque, and produces zero tailpipe emissions, but the electric pickup failed to meet Ford’s expectations because of its higher price.

The base F-150 Lightning Pro debuted in 2021 with a starting MSRP of $39,974, but that was quickly raised to around $60,000 a year or so later.

According to Edmunds.com, the average transaction price for the F-150 Lightning in its first year of sales was $79,000 because Ford focused on higher-priced trims. The gas version’s ATP was about $19,000 less.

Even with the higher sticker price, Ford was losing a considerable amount on each Lightning it produced. In Q1 2024, Ford lost more than $100,000 on every EV it built.

Next year, Ford will take another crack at the electric pickup market with the Fathom, the first vehicle based on its “groundbreaking” new Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform.

Ford said the Fathom will start at $28,350 for the standard-range version. Even with the $1,595 delivery fee included, the electric pickup will start at under $30,000.

As the first vehicle built on its UEV platform, Ford promises the Fathom will be a step-change from its first-generation EVs.

According to Ford, the electric pickup will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4 and will be the first vehicle with Apple Maps directly integrated into the navigation system.

We also know the electric pickup will have a NACS port after a few prototypes were spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger this summer.

Ford reportedly aims to sell around 100,000 Fathoms in its first year. CEO Jim Farley said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week that the launch remains on track for Q4 2027.

Farley called the Fathom a “breakthrough product” and said that the MSRP under $30,000 is perfect for today’s market.

At least some F-150 owners are already trading in for lower-priced options. A member of the Ford F-150 Lightning Owners Group, JF, said that although it was a great ride, “Carvana gave us just a little less than we paid new,” adding, “R2, here we come!”

When Torque News reached out, JF said he “really liked the Lightning,” but wanted something smaller. “With the current increase in resale value, the time to trade seemed right,” JF added.

The Rivian R2 (see our review) Performance with the Launch Package is now available to order starting at $57,990 with an EPA-estimated range of up to 330 miles and 656 hp. The R2 Premium will go on sale later this year, starting at $53,990

In Spring 2027, Rivian will launch the R2 Standard, starting at $44,990 with an estimated range of up to 275 miles and 350 hp.

So were they losing $100k / truck, or the average loss when all development was included ended up being $100k? Big difference. I don't believe the cost to build each one was $170k+. That makes no sense. They just priced them too high to amortize the development costs over enough vehicles to make them profitable. Every vehicle has to sell a minimum # before they start to make a profit.

Surging F-150 Lightning sales on the used market show buyers want electric pickups. But at the right price.

At $60,000 to $70,000, the Lightning wasn’t so attractive, but at $40,000 used, it suddenly is. Perhaps Ford is on to something with its next-gen EV pickup, the Fathom, set to go on sale starting at under $30,000.

Will it deliver on its promise? Ford has yet to reveal battery specs, towing capacity, range, or any other specs. We should learn more soon.

#4553. Audi May Invest an Additional $3 Billion in Georgia Factory: Report

The German automaker just announced its $4 billion plans for its first U.S. plant, but it may already be considering a second phase of construction.

Audi hasn’t even broken ground on its newly announced $4 billion plans for a 1500-acre factory in Macon, Georgia, but the German automaker is already hinted at an additional $3 billion investment in the facility.

A new report from Reuters claims that Audi is already considering a second phase of construction at the Georgia plant. After pledging to invest an initial $4 billion, documents released by the Mid-Georgia Gateway Development Authority reportedly state that Audi will invest $3 billion more by 2033. Audi supposedly aims to employ an additional 3000 workers as part of the expansion plan.

The Trump Administration allegedly promised Audi some degree of tariff relief as part of the decision to build its first U.S. production facility; Reuters reported that Audi pushed for the European Union import duty to be lowered to 7.5 percent, but that the U.S. Commerce Department was expected to agree to around 10 percent. Currently, Audi imports all of its models to the U.S. from Europe and Mexico, and models from the EU are subject to a 15 percent tariff. Audi paid $1.4 billion in duties to the U.S. government last year.

Georgia is heavily incentivizing Audi’s decision to build in the Peach State: it is giving Audi the land, as well as providing $458 million in tax incentives and offering $120 million in grants. These grants will focus on infrastructure, rail improvements, environmental site remediation, and construction, according to Automotive News. The company will also be provided an additional $430 million in subsidies for water, road improvements, utility issues, workforce training, and recruitment.

Audi plans to produce its Q7, Q8, and Q9 SUVs at its future U.S. facilities. The German automaker isn’t limiting its U.S. production plans to Georgia, either: an additional 25,000 Audi units will reportedly be produced at an incoming Scout Motors factory in South Carolina. Audi pledged to build 200,000 vehicles annually at the Georgia plant by the early 2030s.

#4552. Hyundai Has a Clever Way to Add Power to a Two-Way Tailgate

A little transmission would let one drive motor raise and lower the whole tailgate or swing one section sideways.

Multifunction and split tailgates are definitely a thing now, and there’s probably no going back. Many truckmakers offer some sort of door-within-a-door or built-in-step arrangement that adds utility to what was previously just a hinged wall that kept stuff in the bed. A new Hyundai/Kia concept could take that to the next level by applying power to a two-way tailgate.

A recently published U.S. patent application covering a previously disclosed design builds on previous filings that describe a split tailgate that opens two ways: the conventional way, swinging the whole unit down with hinge action at the bottom, or sideways opening, with a vertical hinge allowing a portion of the tailgate to swing out, providing belly-up-to-the-bed access. That much we've seen before.

See all results for used Hyundai for sale near 20147

The distinguishing feature is that this split tailgate can open and close in either direction, and do so with power from a single drive motor. All two-way tailgates currently offered by Ford, Honda, and Ram require manual operation for side-opening, and only Ford’s offers powered raising and lowering. Not only does the Hyundai/Kia idea remove that unnecessary application of work, but it does so with clever simplicity.

Think of the mechanism as a little transmission that sends one drive motor’s power to either of two outputs. One operates the bottom hinge to raise or lower the entire tailgate. The other operates a spindle that pushes or pulls a lever to swing one section sideways. A second motor operates the clutch mechanism that selects between them. So there are two motors, but only one does the work of moving the tailgate.

Sure, you could figure out a way to package two drive motors into such a tailgate or its surroundings, but that’s unnecessary complexity and likely more weight. The latest patent describes control logic that should avoid any expensive crashes. Before beginning either opening sequence, the controller checks that both tailgate latches are engaged and the vehicle is stopped. It then selects the appropriate drive path, releases the corresponding latch, and powers the gate open.

One notable design difference seen in the application’s drawings is that the vertical hinge lives at the seam between the tailgate’s two sections, not on the truck bed as in Honda’s and Ram’s production implementations, and the side-opening portion latches to the truck’s box. Ford also uses a mid-tailgate vertical hinge, but its panel within a panel is surrounded by more tailgate on either side.

See all results for used Hyundai for sale near 20147

If something like this were to make production, it would most likely turn up on the mid-size body-on-frame pickup Hyundai has promised. We’ve also seen a patent for a hardtop for the related SUV that would allow for one-person roof assembly. There’s nothing that says both innovations couldn’t end up on both of the new off-roaders, but of course there's no guarantee of either.

#4551. E-quipment highlight: Jungheinrich launches new forklift for Asian markets

Like many equipment brands, German forklift maker Jungheinrich has been struggling to crack the Asian industrial markets – but the company is set to change all that with the launch of a new line of 1.6- to 3-ton class electric forklifts designed specifically to navigate the region’s tight warehouses and factories.

Jungheinrich launched the next generation of its EFG MB and MC electric counterbalance forklifts, giving businesses more flexibility to match truck performance with the battery options, charging systems, and operator features that meet their specific needs.

“Different operations have different requirements,” said Lisa Jing Xue, Managing Director at Jungheinrich’s Qingpu Plant, China. “With the EFG M series, customers can configure the (forklift) truck around their application, workload and operators – whether they need greater maneuverability for confined warehouse spaces, or a stable, powerful truck for demanding transport and stacking work.”

Forklift buyers can choose between two performance packages, prioritizing energy efficiency for everyday material handling or more driving and lifting muscle for more demanding, high-throughput operations. The higher-performance package comes standard on models rated for 2.5-3.0 tons, with a choice of either lead-acid or lithium-ion batteries with 346 or 690 Ah of capacity available to suit different workloads and shift patterns. Both ship with regenerative braking tech that can recover up to 30% of the energy used in stopping and lowering loads, too, helping to keep these machines running longer between charging sessions.

“We carried out extensive customer research to understand what the market needs,” added Jing Xue. “Customers can invest in the performance required today and add further capabilities as their application demands.”

Optional features include fingertip controls, a larger 4″ digital display, upgraded LED lighting, and operator-assistance (ADAS) systems, while flexible seating and cabin configurations are designed to keep drivers comfortable through long shifts. A slim B-pillar and glass roof help visibility in busy warehouses, while the four-wheel EFG MC gets automatic cornering speed reduction as standard. Integrated telematics are also standard, giving fleet managers access to utilization data, maintenance planning and pre-operational checks from day one.

Jungheinrich says the order books for both the three- and four-wheel electric forklifts are open now, ready to be supported by the company’s 6,000+ person strong service network across the Asia-Pacific region.

Italian leather, custom comfort, and auto-inspired design make these my favorite shoes for Formula 1 weekends.

There’s something fitting about the Model T sneaker becoming my favorite for race weekends. Much like the cars we obsess over, the Iambic Model T takes an engineering-first approach to comfort, combining modern technology, thoughtful construction, and premium materials.

Think of it like commissioning a luxury grand tourer. A Ferrari isn’t simply about horsepower; it’s about the materials, the craftsmanship, and attention to the person behind the wheel. Iambic applies the same philosophy, from its Italian leather to its personalized fit.

After wearing mine throughout the year, across Europe and the U.S., I'm convinced the approach works.

Rather than relying on conventional shoe sizing, Iambic uses AI-assisted technology to create a personalized fit. The process begins with a smartphone app that captures images of your feet and collects information about your comfort preferences. It may seem unusual, but I promise it makes sense. Through the app, you will send pictures of each foot from different angles to capture the full scope and how you stand. That data helps determine how your shoes are made. These foot scans showed me that I wear slightly more on my right side because of an old skating injury, something I never knew.

The Model T is handcrafted in Portugal using Italian full-grain leather, with a triple-layer rubber sole, adjustable foam insoles, and a padded heel collar. It’s an impressive combination.

For someone accustomed to appreciating the details inside a well-appointed Italian automobile, that approach feels familiar. The materials matter, but so does how everything works together.

I’ve worn my white Model Ts all over Modena’s cobblestone streets with my family, through multiple days at racetracks, and across America on my 36-hour Route 66 road trip. They’ve become my favorite driving and racing shoes, and that says a lot.

Anyone who’s attended a race knows how much walking it involves. Between navigating sprawling circuits, standing for hours, and sometimes carrying equipment or bags, your footwear gets a serious workout.

Silverstone was the ultimate test. Four consecutive days of traversing the circuit left my sneakers considerably dirty, but my feet stayed unswollen and blister-free. I didn’t even wear socks with them the last day (so they wouldn’t clash with my Fernando outfit). They were so comfortable that I rarely thought about my feet, even when walking across the hilly, uneven grounds and up and down the grandstand.

They also became my preferred driving shoes for long-haul trips with my cousin. Their fit and manageable sole made hours and hours in the driver’s seat enjoyable, without the bulk of traditional athletic sneakers. And despite the punishment they underwent, a basic leather-cleaning kit brought the white back to life.

At $600, the Model T belongs in the same conversation as other premium footwear, but the appeal goes beyond appearance. You’re investing in personalized construction, a sneaker designed for serious use and only for you. After a full season of travel, mine have more than justified their price.

With Austin, Texas, behind us and Las Vegas approaching, remember that a Grand Prix involves considerably more walking than most first-time attendees anticipate. Every year, social media fills with photos of blistered feet from fans who chose fashionable boots or sleek loafers over comfort. My advice? Save the fancy boots and dress shoes for dinner.

If you’re already investing in the experience of attending a Formula 1 race, or any race, the right footwear makes perfect sense. Like a beautifully engineered Italian sports car, the Iambic Model T proves performance and luxury can coexist.

#4549. Acura Kicks Off Sales of More Than 3000 Official Reproduction Parts for the 1st-Gen NSX

Acura’s NSX heritage parts program moves from announcement to U.S. sales, giving owners fresh support for their aging supercars.

Buying or owning an older supercar is one thing. Keeping it on the road is another issue, and that's only complicated further when it comes to finding replacement parts. Acura is now making that aspect of ownership about as easy as it could possibly be for first-gen NSX owners: this week, the brand is officially kicking off sales of more than 3000 reproduction parts through its Honda Heritage Parts program.

The new welcome development for NSX owners comes through Acura dealerships nationwide and through Honda's DreamShop. The reality here is that, although great cars like the NSX have exceptional enthusiast support, factory-backed parts re-creation is hard to match. It's one thing to hope you'll find a part across used listings and another to know it's available at a local dealer.

If all this sounds familiar, it's for good reason. As Road & Track reported in March, the company has been intending to bring reproduction parts to American dealers for a minute now. This latest development moves the story along to actual sales. That said, there are two very clear sides to this business: “Genuine Honda Reproduction Parts” use the same materials and production methods as the original components; “Honda Compatible Parts” are redeveloped replacements for original pieces that the company no longer sells.

See all results for used Honda for sale near 07104

That differentiation allows the brand to build what it feels makes sense and lean on suppliers elsewhere. Originally, Acura said it would cover the powertrain, interior, exterior, electrical, and chassis components. That's a wide swath to be sure—but for now, owners will still need to check availability to be sure that the individual piece they need is available.

That said, all of this signals just how key the NSX is to Acura and Honda. Supporting a supercar decades after production helps owners keep and maintain the car in question. In addition, it gives prospective buyers a touch more confidence about picking one up. In other words, it could boost the second-hand market and the overarching value of the nameplate itself. That won't make an NSX (or any other supercar) cheap or easy to maintain, but it eases some of the frustration.

#4548. Janus Electric secures battery supply deal for its battery-swap semi truck

Australian conversion specialists Janus Electric have been celebrating a growing slate of orders for their Class 8 electric truck conversions, which ditch diesel in favor of advanced battery-swap electric power – but exactly how they’d deliver all those trucks was still a question. Now, we have an answer: Electrovaya will supply the batteries.

The concept of dropping an electric power unit into a Class 8 semi makes perfect sense, as most of these trucks are built as gliders. That is, rolling body and chassis without an engine and transmission that’s ready to receive power from Cummins, Detroit, International, or Volvo Penta. That’s the role that Janus Electric sees itself occupying, and it seems to be working.

Janus’ reservation book crept past 70 units this past summer, helped along in part by California’s HVIP Program and the US EPA’s Diesel Emission Reduction Act (DERA) Grants. When the HVIP voucher is combined with the Port of Los Angeles’ “Plus” support, customers can received up to $166,000 per truck conversion. Factor in the massive fuel savings of electric and the classic good looks of square-nose Western Star truck body, and it’s easy to see why they’d be a popular choice.

As Jerry Seinfeld taught us however, it’s one thing to take a reservation – it’s another thing to deliver. To help make it happen, Janus has inked a battery supply deal with Electrovaya that will see a $26 million initial purchase orders for Electrovaya battery packs to demand for Janus’ products in the US and Canada, along with the battery company purchasing approximately $1.4 million in Janus stock with (what seems to be) actual money.

“Electrovaya is an important partner to Janus Electric, and we’re particularly pleased it has decided to invest directly in our business,” explains Ben Hutt, Managing Director and CEO of Janus Electric. “The investment is a strong vote of confidence in our technology and approach to electrifying heavy transport.”

The Janus Electric-repowered trucks carry a stout, 480 hp electric motor drawing power from a standard 310 kWh battery pack, with up to two battery packs (one on each side) of the truck. In practice, that gives the Janus trucks up to 370 miles of loaded range. After that, the batteries can be DC fast charged in under 90 minutes, or swapped for fresh ones in about four minutes without too much in the way of specialized equipment. That’s not just Janus’ killer app, it means that a battery supply deal like this one with a strategic partner who’s invested in the fledgling company’s success is such a huge deal.

“Reliable battery supply is critical to our growth,” adds Hutt, “and Electrovaya’s expanding North American manufacturing capabilities will be important as we scale. Both companies see considerable opportunity in this market, and we look forward to building on our partnership.”

For their part, Electrovoya executives seem to know their role here, and seem excited to be a part of what Janus is doing. “Class 8 trucking is one of the most exciting and demanding frontiers in electrification, and Janus has demonstrated real commercial traction with fleets in the US, Canada and Australia,” said Dr. Raj Das Gupta, CEO of Electrovaya. “Janus has developed a practical solution to one of the major challenges facing heavy transport, enabling diesel-powered trucks to be converted to electric without compromising their commercial operations.”

Electrovaya will be expanding its American manufacturing capacity with lithium-ion cell, module, and battery pack production at its new, potentially BABA-compliant facility in Jamestown, New York, which is expected to come online in 2027.

#4547. EVs Made Up Nearly A Third Of UK Sales As Europe's Electric Boom Continues

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

While EV sales are growing slowly in the U.S., despite the loss of federal tax incentives, they're exploding in the UK. According to UK's car industry lobby New Automotive, 49,155 new fully battery-electric vehicles (BEV) were sold in October. That's not only a massive 54% increase over last October, but it's 32% of the UK's new car market share, or almost a third.

That 32% market share also gave EVs the largest market share of any one fuel type, more than gas, diesel, or hybrids. "Almost one in three new cars sold in October was fully electric, more than any other fuel type, and electric car sales are up by more than half on last year," said Ben Nelmes, CEO at New AutoMotive. "Drivers are voting with their wallets. Every one of those new electric cars means a household spending less on running costs, and a country less exposed to the oil price shock."

There's more EV variety in the UK than there is in America. The UK has access to EVs from brands like Renault, Peugeot, Fiat, Volkswagen, Skoda, and even Chinese EVs like BYD and Jaecoo. Last month, Kia, BMW, Volkswagen, and BYD led the country's electric market. Tesla slumped after a big September.

Year-to-date, though, Tesla is number one, with 9.53% market share. That's up 25.4% from last year, too. Kia took second place, with 6.9% market share, and BYD came in third, with 6.8%. What's surprising is that no European EV brands were in the top three, despite being in their home continent. I'd sell a non-essential organ for a Renault 5 E-Tech, so I'm surprised to see cars like that not taking top spots in the UK.

It isn't just new EVs, either. The UK is also seeing a jump in used EVs, just like we are here. According to EV Powered, data shows that more and more UK customers are shopping for used EVs.

The run up in oil costs is driving record EV sales across Europe. BEVs took 37% share of the car market in Germany, the country's road traffic agency said, with over 94,000 vehicles sold. That's a nearly 80% increase year over year.

#4546. Energica rises from the ashes with plans for cheaper electric motorcycles

The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under new international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around.

Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.

Energica says motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy. The new manufacturing setup is expected to significantly reduce production costs, allowing Energica to cut motorcycle prices by around 20% compared to its previous models.

That could be a big deal for a company whose motorcycles were widely praised for their performance and technology, but were also firmly positioned at the premium end of the market.

The revival comes after Energica was acquired by Energica Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-based company backed by international private investors. Importantly, much of the technological know-how isn’t disappearing overseas with the manufacturing. Energica says its core engineering and design leadership remains in Italy, including longtime CTO Giampiero Testoni and designer Paolo Imeni.

The first motorcycle to make its comeback will be the Energica Experia, the company’s adventure-oriented electric sport-tourer. After that, Energica plans to progressively restart production of the Ego, Eva Ribelle, and EsseEsse9, eventually bringing its entire previous lineup back to market.

At least initially, those motorcycles will use their existing platforms, which should help Energica get bikes rolling off the production line faster without having to develop and homologate entirely new machines. But upgrades are already planned, including a new battery and improvements to range, efficiency, performance, and reliability.

Energica is also specifically targeting Europe, the United States, and Australia as it rebuilds its dealer and service networks. Existing owners haven’t been forgotten either. The company says service has already resumed and spare-parts shipments have restarted to dealers in several countries.

For anyone who followed the electric motorcycle industry over the last decade, Energica’s disappearance was a particularly painful one. This wasn’t some startup with a couple of renderings and a dream. Energica built some of the highest-performance electric motorcycles on the road and spent four seasons supplying the motorcycles for the FIM MotoE World Cup, experience that helped develop its high-voltage and DC fast-charging technology.

Now the company gets something relatively rare in the motorcycle industry: a second chance.

And if moving production to Asia really can knock around 20% off Energica’s prices while retaining the Italian engineering that made the bikes special in the first place, Energica 2.0 might have a considerably better shot at turning great electric motorcycles into a sustainable business.

It seems like moving toward Asian manufacturing is all but inevitable here. It was the expensive European manufacturing of low-volume motorcycles that weighed so heavily on Energica’s balance sheets in the years up to their financial troubles, and so shifting production to countries with both the expertise and the cost benefits for motorcycle manufacturing simply makes sense.

Energica isn’t alone in discovering the economics of moving electric motorcycle production to Asia. Zero Motorcycles spent years manufacturing its bikes in California before beginning a major shift toward production in the Philippines in 2023, including both complete motorcycles and major subassemblies. Now the company works with multiple factories, including major manufacturers like Zongshen in China, to reduce production costs for its electric motorcycles while still maintaining the ‘designed in California’ marketing angle.

It’s too early to tell how the new strategy will play out for Energica, but the fact that the company is now following a more well-worn trail is a positive sign for those who have spent the last two years hoping for a revival.

#4545. Mitsubishi Releases More Specs on the Pajero SUV, Including Pricing

This three-row 4x4 could be a legitimate 4Runner or Land Cruiser competitor once Mitsubishi officially decides to revive the Montero and bring this off-roader to the U.S.

Mitsubishi’s new Pajero SUV looks like a legitimate competitor to the Toyota 4Runner and Land Cruiser, now that we have the full specs on this new off-road-oriented SUV. It’s set to go on sale in Japan next month, and while Mitsubishi says it still hasn’t reached a decision about U.S. availability, its dimensions and pricing put it in line with Toyota’s popular mid-size SUVs.

The Pajero measures 193.7 inches long, 75.8 inches wide, and 75.2 inches tall. Those measurements are all within a few inches of the 4Runner, though the Mitsu is narrower overall. It has three rows of seats and seating for seven, and it’s built on a ladder frame and has standard four-wheel drive.

See all results for new 2028 Mitsubishi Montero for sale near 94043

The powertrain for the Japanese market is a 2.4-liter turbo-diesel inline-four with 201 horsepower and 354 pound-feet of torque. That engine is unlikely to make its way to the U.S., but we do like the idea of a torquey diesel off-roader with decent fuel economy—Mitsubishi claims 28 mpg on the WLTP cycle.

Though Japan-market pricing isn’t an indicator of what this model could cost if it comes to the States, we do know that the Pajero starts at the equivalent of $39,000 and goes up to $50,000 for the loaded Super Exceed trim level pictured here.
